comparator.name: International Relations and International Organization
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page and 2026-2027 Ocasys curriculum define a redesigned three-year, 180-EC bachelor. Years 1 and 2 each contain 60 EC of compulsory international-relations, history, politics, economics, law, methods and a continuous 20-EC modern-language sequence. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine minor, study-abroad or career-minor space, one 10-EC faculty-wide IMPACT choice, a 10-EC IRIO specialization module and a 10-EC independent bachelor thesis. The open choices are preserved generically and the coherent pathway totals exactly 180 EC.

alternatives.label: International Relations, Organisations and Political Economy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines political science and international-relations theory with international and EU law, economics, global history, quantitative and qualitative methods, and communication. The label reflects its balanced IRIO core without presenting one supporting discipline as the whole programme.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to Groningen IRIO: a broad programme in international-relations theory, international organisations and law, comparative politics, EU governance, conflict and security, international political economy, global history, and quantitative and qualitative research. UCR assembles this through several disciplines and cannot reproduce the comparator’s dedicated IRIO sequence or compulsory language training.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is earlier: GOSGATE102 in semester 1 precedes all selected advanced law courses, and BENGATE102 in semester 2 precedes all selected economics courses that require it. Personal & Professional Development is in semester 2. Introductory politics, law and economics precede advanced EU politics, political economy, econometrics and conflict study; research methods precedes Econometrics; rhetoric precedes Persuasive Communication; and Theory of International Relations precedes European Union Politics and Peace & Conflict. Every course is offered in its assigned term for the Fall 2026 cohort.

alternatives.label: International Security, Law and Global Governance
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum shifts five courses from general economics, sociology and communication into criminal and EU law, security history, extremism, data science and an advanced research seminar. The label states that narrower concentration accurately.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different route concentrating on threats to international order and the institutions used to govern them: peace and conflict, organised crime and radicalisation, public international and EU law, human rights, comparative constitutional systems, security history, and quantitative, qualitative and data-science methods.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is earlier: GOSGATE102 in semester 1 precedes international, criminal, constitutional and EU law, and BENGATE102 in semester 2 precedes International Macroeconomics and Econometrics. Personal & Professional Development is in semester 2. Introductory political, legal and economic study precedes advanced EU politics, conflict, extremism, machine learning and the research seminar; Introduction to Data Science precedes Machine Learning. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: This concentration replaces Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Persuasive Communication and Introduction to Sociology with Criminal Law & Criminal Justice, History Research Seminar, Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning and Youth Resilience to Extremism. The programmes differ by five courses (37.5 EC) each way, above the 30-EC floor, and the changes follow directly from the security, law and data-governance concept.

alternatives.label: Climate Governance, Sustainability and International Cooperation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines eight environmental and sustainability courses with international relations, EU politics, public international law, economics, empirical methods, climate communication, ethics and environmental justice. The environmental-governance organising logic dominates and is reflected in the label.
alternatives.concept: A genuinely different third route built from the programme’s explicit question why states struggle to cooperate on global environmental problems. It makes climate and sustainability science the substantive core and connects that evidence to international-relations theory, comparative and EU politics, public international law, economics, data analysis, policy, communication, ethics and environmental justice.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is earlier: ENSGATE101 in semester 1 precedes Sustainability Essentials II, Renewable System Design, R3 and Environmental Biogeochemistry; GOSGATE102 precedes Public International Law; and BENGATE102 precedes International Macroeconomics and Public Economics. Personal & Professional Development is in semester 2. Climate Change, sustainability foundations, economics and law precede advanced renewable systems, sustainability governance, environmental science, EU politics, environmental justice and conflict. Every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: This environmental-governance route shares 11 of 24 courses with each of the first two alternatives and therefore differs by 13 courses (97.5 EC) each way, well above the floor. Its renewable systems, circular economy, sustainability governance, environmental science, applied sustainability research, climate communication, ethics and environmental-justice courses are direct curricular consequences of the climate-cooperation concept, not arbitrary substitutions.

selection.assessment: Three UCR alternatives are defensible and the maximum is reached. The closest match owns the target’s broad international-relations, international-organisation, global-politics, EU, law, economics, history, research and interdependence interests (104-108, 111-112, 116, 125 and 127). Security (114, supported by 115 and 126) forms a coherent law-and-governance concentration and passes feasibility and five-course distinctness. Climate cooperation and environmental governance (109-110, supported by 113 and 126) form a second coherent direction and produce a sustainability-led curriculum that differs from both other alternatives by 13 courses. The language direction (124) is evidenced but cannot independently support a 24-course programme because the current UCR workbook contains no modern-language course; the comparator’s language limitation is stated explicitly. Curricular-topic rows 113, 115, 117 and 126 support the core or candidates, while outcome rows 118-123 remain search-only.

blocks: This is genuine approved minor, study-abroad or career-minor space and has no universal subject content to match.
The comparator allows one of several faculty-wide thematic courses, so no single subject can be aligned without inventing a choice.
International relations, organisations and political systems
Both develop theory-led analysis of political power and order; UCR approaches it through political philosophy rather than a second IR survey.
Both establish comparative concepts for analysing political systems and institutions.
Both introduce international-relations theories and their use in explaining state behaviour and international order.
Both examine European Union institutions, decision-making and political pressures; the Groningen unit also integrates law.
International Relations Today is a separately credited current-affairs unit; the scheduled UCR politics courses cannot be counted twice.
Law, European governance, security and conflict
Both study public international law and the institutional architecture of international cooperation.
Both directly examine conflict, security, violence and peacebuilding.
International Macroeconomics directly supports analysis of cross-border economic interdependence and political economy.
Both connect economic analysis to public policy and collective choices.
Both provide modern historical context for contemporary world politics; UCR offers a broader modern-history course.
Both use long-run historical power structures to explain modern international relations; UCR focuses on empires.
Both require advanced tutorial-style research; UCR applies it in a history seminar rather than an IRIO specialization.
The comparator requires an independent bachelor thesis; UCR’s standardized Optional independent research element is shown in this row rather than treating a scheduled course as a thesis.
Both introduce statistics and empirical research design for social-science questions.
Both train research design and method; UCR focuses on qualitative social-science methodology.
The comparator requires a modern-language sequence; the current UCR workbook contains no equivalent modern-language course.
The compulsory language continuation has no equivalent scheduled UCR course.
Both examine major global change; UCR concentrates specifically on climate change.

notes.text: Groningen IRIO provides a dedicated two-year sequence in international relations, organisations, history, economics, law, methods and compulsory modern-language study, followed by a specialization module and bachelor thesis. UCR offers closely related politics, law, economics, history, sociology, communication, sustainability and research courses, but its programmes are assembled across disciplines and do not reproduce the integrated IRIO sequence or language requirement.

The Groningen programme includes 30 EC of approved minor or study-abroad space, a faculty-wide thematic choice, an IRIO specialization tutorial and an integrated thesis. UCR distributes comparable subject matter across its open curriculum; the standardized Optional independent research element indicates a possible research opportunity without treating a scheduled UCR course as the comparator thesis.
